test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: When starting balance is debit, i.e., favourable balance as per cash book, identify which of the following transactions will be added ?

options.text: Wrong credit granted by the bank
Direct payment by the bank as per standing instruction

solution:
The correct answer is **Wrong credit granted by the bank.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wrong credit granted by the bank:**

 
 
• This transaction involves the bank erroneously crediting an amount to the company's account, increasing the balance in the cash book.
 
• Since the starting balance is a debit (favourable balance), this wrong credit will be added to reconcile the balance as per the cash book with the bank statement.
 
• This adjustment is necessary to reflect the true balance after accounting for the bank's error.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cheque recorded but not deposited:**

 
 
• This would not be added but subtracted. If a cheque is recorded in the cash book but not deposited in the bank, it means the cash book shows more balance than the bank statement.
 
 
 
• **Bill of exchange dishonoured:**
 
 
• This would be subtracted. If a bill of exchange is dishonoured, it means the expected payment was not received, reducing the balance in the cash book.
 
 
 
• **Direct payment by the bank as per standing instruction:**
 
 
• This would be subtracted. Direct payments by the bank, such as standing instructions for utility bills, would reduce the balance in the bank statement but may not immediately be reflected in the cash book.
